name: evidence and oracle science
owns: how a claim is proven: what counts as an oracle, how a false positive is excluded, how a result is reproduced, and what a captured artefact has to carry to be worth anything
why_in_D: This lens decides whether anything in the other fifteen is true. A finding without a negative control is a hypothesis. A timing difference without a false positive rate is noise. A screenshot without the request that produced it is an assertion. Every other lens produces claims, and this is the only lens that decides which claims survive scepticism.

factors.name: oracle definition per class
factors.def: the specific observable that distinguishes success from failure for this class
factors.observable: a state change visible without trusting the response body

factors.name: negative control presence
factors.def: whether the same procedure was run with the malicious element removed and produced no effect
factors.observable: no effect in the control condition

factors.name: differential comparison
factors.def: whether two conditions differ only in the element under test
factors.observable: a difference attributable to one variable

factors.name: false positive rate estimate
factors.def: how often the oracle fires without a real condition
factors.observable: oracle triggers on known negative samples

factors.name: reproducibility from a clean state
factors.def: whether the result holds on a fresh environment with only the documented steps
factors.observable: a second run by a second party

factors.name: timing measurement resolution
factors.def: whether the clock resolution and jitter allow the claimed distinction
factors.observable: separation larger than the measured noise

factors.name: statistical power of a timing claim
factors.def: whether enough samples were taken for the effect size claimed
factors.observable: a p value or effect size reported with n

factors.name: blind analysis
factors.def: whether the analyst knew the expected answer while looking
factors.observable: a procedure that hides the condition from the scorer

factors.name: confirmation criterion pre registration
factors.def: whether the success condition was fixed before the test
factors.observable: a criterion stated in advance

factors.name: artefact capture completeness
factors.def: whether the full request, response, timestamp and host are recorded
factors.observable: a capture sufficient to replay

factors.name: capture integrity
factors.def: whether the artefact is hashed at capture and unchanged since
factors.observable: a hash recorded with the artefact

factors.name: timestamp source and accuracy
factors.def: whether the clock is trustworthy and in a stated timezone
factors.observable: a clock offset measured against a reference

factors.name: environment description adequacy
factors.def: whether the runtime, version, network position and configuration are recorded
factors.observable: a third party able to rebuild the environment

factors.name: attribution to a request
factors.def: whether a server side effect can be tied to the specific request that caused it
factors.observable: a correlation identifier spanning both sides

factors.name: side effect avoidance
factors.def: whether the proof changed state that should not have changed
factors.observable: a reversible action taken where possible

factors.name: minimum proof principle
factors.def: whether the least invasive action that still proves the claim was used
factors.observable: an action larger than needed

factors.name: severity versus proof separation
factors.def: whether impact is argued separately from the demonstrated fact
factors.observable: a claim of impact labelled as inference

factors.name: assumption inventory
factors.def: whether every unverified premise is listed
factors.observable: an assumption not marked as such

factors.name: worst case versus demonstrated case
factors.def: whether the report distinguishes what was shown from what might follow
factors.observable: a demonstrated limit stated explicitly

factors.name: false negative risk
factors.def: whether absence of a finding means absent or merely not tried
factors.observable: a test coverage statement

factors.name: oracle independence from the interface
factors.def: whether success is confirmed through a channel other than the one attacked
factors.observable: confirmation by direct store read or second client

factors.name: cache and CDN interference with results
factors.def: whether an intermediary served the response, making the result about the cache
factors.observable: a cache hit header on the decisive request

factors.name: load balancer variance across attempts
factors.def: whether attempts hit different backends and produced different answers
factors.observable: divergent results correlated with backend identity

factors.name: state contamination between tests
factors.def: whether an earlier test changed the state that the later one measured
factors.observable: different result after a reset

factors.name: rate limiting interference
factors.def: whether the test was throttled and the throttle mistaken for a behaviour
factors.observable: status changes consistent with a limit

factors.name: waf normalisation of the probe
factors.def: whether the defence altered the payload so the result is about the defence
factors.observable: a payload echoed in altered form

factors.name: client versus server enforcement split
factors.def: whether the control tested is the client's, and therefore bypassable by a different client
factors.observable: the same action accepted from a raw client

factors.name: authorisation versus authentication confusion
factors.def: whether a positive result is authenticated access rather than an authorisation failure
factors.observable: the acting principal recorded

factors.name: self impact versus cross principal impact
factors.def: whether the effect touches only the tester's own data
factors.observable: a second principal affected

factors.name: data sensitivity classification of the finding
factors.def: what exactly was exposed, at which classification
factors.observable: the field names and their classification

factors.name: exploit reliability
factors.def: the fraction of attempts that succeed
factors.observable: success count over attempts

factors.name: precondition fragility
factors.def: how unusual the required configuration is
factors.observable: the configuration prerequisites listed

factors.name: detection likelihood
factors.def: whether the action would have been logged or alerted
factors.observable: presence in telemetry

factors.name: evidence retention duration
factors.def: how long the artefact remains valid, given link rot and rotation
factors.observable: the artefact still retrievable after the engagement

factors.name: redaction completeness
factors.def: whether secrets were removed from the report without removing the proof
factors.observable: a redacted artefact that still demonstrates the point

factors.name: replay of the proof
factors.def: whether the client can reproduce the effect from the artefact alone
factors.observable: a replay by the client

factors.name: oracle stability across time of day
factors.def: whether the effect holds outside the test window
factors.observable: the same result at a different hour

factors.name: geographic variance
factors.def: whether the result depends on network position
factors.observable: a different result from another region

factors.name: account state variance
factors.def: whether the result depends on the tester's account age, plan or role
factors.observable: the result re tested on a fresh account

factors.name: oracle for absence
factors.def: how absence of a control is proven rather than assumed
factors.observable: a positive test of the control that should exist

factors.name: differential between two tenants
factors.def: whether cross tenant effect is shown by reading tenant B's record from tenant A's session
factors.observable: a record whose ownership is not yours

factors.name: differential between two roles
factors.def: whether the effect is shown with the lowest role that reaches it
factors.observable: the same effect from a lower privileged account

factors.name: chained capability transfer
factors.def: whether a chain transfers a capability rather than merely following links
factors.observable: a capability held after step two that was not held after step zero

factors.name: chain step necessity
factors.def: whether every step in a chain was required
factors.observable: the chain failing when a step is removed

factors.name: side channel signal to noise
factors.def: whether the covert signal exceeds environmental noise
factors.observable: repeated decoding of a known value

factors.name: statistical test choice
factors.def: whether the test matches the distribution assumed
factors.observable: a stated test and its assumptions

factors.name: multiple comparison correction
factors.def: whether many probes were counted as many findings
factors.observable: the number of hypotheses tested

factors.name: replication by an independent party
factors.def: whether anyone other than the finder reproduced it
factors.observable: a second confirmation

factors.name: disproof criterion
factors.def: what result would show the finding is wrong
factors.observable: a stated falsifier

factors.name: vendor confirmation alignment
factors.def: whether the vendor's fix addresses the demonstrated mechanism or a symptom
factors.observable: the patch matching the report

factors.name: regression test after fix
factors.def: whether the original proof fails after the fix and the control still passes
factors.observable: the exploit refused, the feature working

factors.name: bypass of the fix
factors.def: whether the fix covers the class or one instance
factors.observable: a variant that still works

factors.name: oracle cost
factors.def: the requests, time or money required per bit learned
factors.observable: measured cost per successful extraction

factors.name: noise injection defence
factors.def: whether the defender adds noise that degrades the oracle, and its measured effect
factors.observable: signal quality before and after the defence

factors.name: rate limiting effect on extraction
factors.def: whether a limit changes the viability of a slow oracle
factors.observable: requests per hour versus bits per hour

factors.name: honeypot discrimination
factors.def: whether the target is a decoy, which invalidates the whole finding
factors.observable: signs of planted data or unusual uniformity

factors.name: reported versus actual scope of a test
factors.def: whether the report states what was not tested
factors.observable: an explicit out of scope list

factors.name: oracle for a blind write
factors.def: how a write with no readback is confirmed
factors.observable: a second order read or an error shape change

factors.name: oracle for a resource exhaustion
factors.def: how exhaustion is distinguished from throttling
factors.observable: latency and error shape under increasing load

factors.name: oracle for information exposure
factors.def: how existence is shown without retrieving the content
factors.observable: a length, status or timing difference

factors.name: confidence statement
factors.def: whether the report states how sure it is and why
factors.observable: an explicit confidence with its basis

factors.name: cost of being wrong
factors.def: what happens operationally if the finding is false
factors.observable: a rollback plan for the fix

factors.name: measurement of the measurement
factors.def: whether the tool used to observe was itself validated
factors.observable: a known positive detected by the observer

factors.name: oracle independence across two engines
factors.def: whether two unrelated tools agree, which is the only defence against a single tool's assumption
factors.observable: the same conclusion from a second implementation
